rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Game Turn 1.1 Play 1 Marker 1.2 Reclaim markers 2 Display Fossil 3 Score Points 4 End of the Game Game Turn Starting with the first player, players take turns in clockwise order. On your turn, you must do one of these two actions: Play 1 Marker To play 1 marker, at least 1 marker must be on your board. If you have no markers on your board, then you must do the “reclaim markers” action. Take 1 of the markers from your board and place it at a Dig Site that does not already contain one of your markers. Take 1 of the 2 cards from that Dig Site and place it in your Study (i.e. above your board). Apply that card’s effect and any relevant recurring effects Some cards have recurring effects. These effects are applied every time that condition is met, including at the moment you actually take the card. Most cards have a single use effect, which only occurs once, during the turn in which you take the card. If multiple effects for cards in your study would trigger at the same time, resolve them in the order of your choice. If effects from multiple players’ cards would trigger at the same time, resolve them in turn order, starting with all the active player’s effects and proceeding clockwise. Finally, refill the open Dig Site space with the top card of the deck. Reclaim markers To reclaim markers, at least 1 of your markers must be at a Dig Site. If you have no markers at any Dig Sites, then you must do the “play 1 marker” action. Take all your markers from Dig Sites and return them to your board. For each marker reclaimed, choose 1 of the following effects: Gain 1 amber Display 1 fossil You can choose a different effect for each marker reclaimed, in any order you wish. Display Fossil To put a fossil on display, spend the amount of amber equal to its size (1, 2, or 3). After spending amber, take the card from your Study and place it facedown below your board. If you cannot pay a fossil’s cost, you cannot put it on display. A fossil on display loses all its effects. When you put a fossil on display, you can either start a new set or expand an existing set: To start a new set, place the card into a new row below your board. Starting a new set does not earn you any points; to earn points, you must expand your set. Once a fossil has been assigned to a set, it must stay there. It cannot later be reassigned to another set. To expand an existing set, add the card to that set. There are two general types of sets: Same Family + different Sizes = Family set Same Size + different Families = Size set Note that the second card added to the set determines its type, and once a set’s type has been defined, it cannot be changed. You cannot add cards of a different Family to a Family set, nor can you add a card to a Family set if the set already contains that card’s Size. You cannot add cards of a different Size to a Size set, nor can you add a card to a Size set if the set already contains that card’s Family. Score Points Each time you expand a set, take 1 Set token from the supply and place it with its 2 points side visible, such that it overlaps the previous card and the new card. Additionally, if you are the first player to expand a set of a particular type, you immediately take from the supply the News token matching that set. If another player obtains the same type of set with more cards, they steal the matching News token! A complete Family set cannot exceed 3 cards, and a complete Size set cannot exceed 5 cards. If you are the first player to complete a type of set, the matching News token can no longer be stolen from you. When you have completed a set, flip over each Set token on that set to their 3 points side. End of the Game The end of the game is triggered when a player takes the last Set token from the supply or when the deck is empty after a player refills a Dig Site. Take all remaining Set tokens from the box and add them to the supply. Play continues until all players have had an equal number of turns, at which point the game ends; then add up your scores. News tokens are worth 3 or 5 points (as indicated on the token). Each Set token is worth 2 points if the set is incomplete or 3 points if the set is complete. Finally, add all the points earned during the game. The player with the most points wins the game! In case of a tie, tied players share victory.

[Rating: 1/10] Elysium (2015, Space Cowboys) with a new theme. Should have reprint it and give it an expansion. What a waste

[Rating: 1/10] Multiplayer Solitaire: waiting for others to do their chores, so you can get in line to do your own chores. It's just a bunch of matrices of this and that. I assumed it was a ripoff of Wingspan, but looking it up I notice it's based on an earlier game about greek mythology. I mean I guess with this scoring system, it could be about literally anything. You're just clueless managers sorting exhibits. I mean I guess Wingspan was the same thing, it could be about anything in the world, since it had no theme.

[Rating: 3/10] A simplified version of Elysium that doesn't seem to get much right. It takes a good game and turns it into an uninteresting exercise.

[Rating: 3/10] Das Spiel sieht nach mehr aus, als es ist. Das Design, die Größe der Schachtel und das Gewicht suggerierten eine Verwandtschaft mit Spielen wie Flügelschlag und Nature; das Spielgeschehen erinnert aber an ein 15€-Amigo-Kartenspiel. Viel zu teuer und zu groß, für das, was es ist. Es ist die Zeit und das Geld nicht wert.

[Rating: 3.5/10] Tried on BGA and found it to be a sad reimplementation of Elysium both in art style and gameplay. No interest in future plays

[Rating: 4/10] Meh, more set collection with lots of iconography to learn and check as new cards come out, lots of effects that trigger off what other players do. For me, all that diluted the interesting aspects of competing over critical cards you need to complete your sets and racing to be in the lead for most cards of the different set types.  I have only vague memory of playing Elysium ages ago, but looking at those cards, Elysium looks much better to me.

[Rating: 4/10] Fairly dull game.  A lot of people are comparing this to Elysium, which I haven't played since it came out more than ten years ago, but I don't see much similarity. In Elysium there was constant tension as your options were more and more limited each time you used up a column. Here, you just take turns putting out tokens to gain cards, then spend a turn regaining your tokens. A lot of the cards do the same thing, so there's usually not a lot of reason to reset your tokens early.  For a game this straightforward, there's also a good amount of unintuitive icons. The combination of dull gameplay 

[Rating: 4/10] Taking from the middle, trying to build a small engine, before converting into point. Not easy to get some grip on the luck of draw.

[Rating: 4.6/10] Simple set collection with a bit of card abilities.  The abilities themselves are not that interesting, but seems like a solid little family game.  I could imagine a kid who's into dinosaurs really liking this.

[Rating: 5/10] First Impressions - 5/28/26 - card combo drafting game with set collection...basic mechanics and nothing that wants me to keep playing - like the unique theme but not the game play experience - for a quicker card game, i prefer fewer tokens and iconography

You need to move the dinosaurs below in order to score points based on sets of the same dinosaur (in each of the 3 sizes) or a set of sizes (in each of the 5 different dinosaurs).
